summary: The Manual Q&A on Tough and Balanced gives opposite orders for a Tough mod on a Balanced unit. Its first sentence says Tough "augmented onto" a Balanced unit is doubled, then balanced; its last sentence says Tough "applied to" a Balanced unit is balanced, then doubled. R19 says the order between printed, mod-given and column-shared attributes is the engine's own call, and the engine balances first.

sides.quote: “Tough” is augmented onto a “Balanced” unit, or if a
will have its defense doubled, then its stats balanced.
If “Tough” is applied to a “Balanced” unit, it will have
its stats balanced, then its defense doubled.
Engine call: the Manual doesn't specify an order for printed-vs-granted-vs-shared;

resolution: Question for the owner. The Manual's words support two readings: (A) "augmented onto" is the mod case and means doubled, then balanced, while "applied to" is some other grant, so the engine's order (R19) is wrong for an augment (F-U16-4); (B) the two sentences describe the same case and contradict each other, so the top-to-bottom principle decides, and where a mod sits relative to the card it is on is unstated. The rule states both and the engine's order.

summary: The Manual lists Inverted as its own layer after the attribute layer, and R226 makes the result independent of grant order. Caleb, quoted in R93, said "Tough inverted balanced would be different" from Tough balanced inverted, which reads as Inverted taking a place inside layer 4.

sides.quote: counters, 4. Attributes like Tough, 5. Inverted, 6.Unaware
Tough inverted balanced would be different
Order-independence is the substantive claim

resolution: Question for the owner. Caleb's words have two real readings: (A) Inverted applies at its place in layer 4's order and inverts only what came before it, so grant order changes the result; (B) a passing remark about a case he called "basically impossible" in the same thread, with Inverted a clean layer after all of layer 4, as the Manual lists. The rule states (B), the Manual's order, which the engine implements.

summary: What happens to two base stats exchanged by Body Swap when the Aberrant Statweaver that set one of them later leaves play is unruled in the RAQ thread.

resolution: Not stated. The rule says only what the thread answers: the exchange takes the base stats as they are when it resolves, and wins over the earlier rewrite. Question for the owner only if the designer does not rule. (Same open thread as D-U05-5.)

summary: The sources are silent on where an effect that switches power and defense applies in the stat layers. The Manual's six layers include no switch, and R66 calls the engine's handling an approximation and the question an open ruling.

sides.quote: Where a real switch belongs is an OPEN RULING, and this line previously guessed
A: Stats have 6 layers to them, which are applied in

summary: The sources are silent on a general dependency rule: how one continuous effect that changes whether another applies is ordered against it. They give only the layer order, timestamps within a layer, and one case (two static strippers whose sources strip each other).

sides.quote: static-vs-static still resolves in one pass
A: Stats have 6 layers to them, which are applied in

resolution: No dependency rule is written. 709 states the layer order and timestamps; 712 states the two-strippers case. Recorded so the judge's CR, if it has a dependency rule, is compared against nothing rather than against an invented one.

summary: R341 says text a copy inherits is as old as the copy's printed text, so any strip takes it. The RAQ says an attribute or ability a unit gains after a strip is not taken. The two part only for a copy that begins on a unit already stripped.

sides.quote: so it is exactly as old as the copy's printed text (R328)
if any unit in play later gains Attribute or Ability, then timestamps takes precedence

resolution: For Borrower of Forms the two agree: it enters play already a copy, so no strip on it is older than its copied text. They differ for an until-regroup copy (Apex Prime) made on a unit already under Suppression Field or Formless. Question for the owner only if that case arises: (A) a copy redefines what the unit prints, so the earlier strip takes the copied text (R341's words); (B) becoming a copy is gaining abilities later, so the earlier strip does not take them (the RAQ's "later gains"). The rule states R341, which is what the sources say about copies.

summary: Whether a unit that has gone to counterattack still counts as an ally in the region it left. R270 states the current answer (it does not) and itself names this as the question the owner should rule on.

sides.quote: does a unit that is out counterattacking still count as an ally in

resolution: Question for the owner. The rule states R270's current answer, which follows the Manual's statement that a counterattacker does not exist until round 1 ends; R270 records that a player who sends two units out together may report it again.

summary: In the same RAQ thread, a source that has left play remembers its formation (Hooba-Bot, Hooba-Pon, Hooba-Lin, Embermaw Fledgling, Lumengrove Lurker), but Flamebreath Initiate counts 0 adjacent allies. The thread does not say why neighbours are not remembered when the formation is.

If Flamebreath Initiate is removed with his trigger on the stack, the X=0 so he will still make Fireball 1.

resolution: Both designer answers are stated as given (714.4 and 714.5). Recorded so a judge's CR that remembers adjacency, or forgets the formation, is compared against both.

summary: That a unit stolen during a battle stays out of formation until regroup, attacking and blocking for nobody, is the owner's call on Download. No printed or designer source covers it, and R8 had said the stolen unit joins its new controller's formations.

sides.quote: including joining the new controller's formations

summary: The owner's words in R152 ("a token ... ceases to exist in all zones other than in play/stack whenever SBAs are checked"), read literally, would send a token mod through a bin before it ceases to exist. resolution: The rule states the token sweep for token bodies; a token mod ceasing to exist is 410.4c (R69). Question for the owner only if the judge's CR sends a token mod through a bin.

summary: Whether a unit stripped by a continuous effect (Transmogrifant, Monke) stops applying its own static abilities. Printed text strips all abilities and R62 says a static is an ability; R62 and R328 encode static-vs-static in one pass that reads only the one-time stamp, so such a unit keeps applying its statics. R62 justifies the one pass only by the mutual case.

a spell stops radiating immediately, while two Monkes — each the other's
**Unchanged:** static-vs-static still resolves in one pass (`staticsFor` reads only

resolution: Printed text outranks our rulings, so the rule states that the unit stops applying its statics, keeps the mutual case as R62 answers it (effects.stripping.mutual), and files the engine's behaviour as F-U16-3. Question for the owner only if R62's one-pass sentence was meant to rule the one-sided case as well.

summary: The sources are silent on whether deaths are checked part-way through an effect's resolution. R313 makes the end of every action a safe point and says a suspended action is not at one; it does not say whether the effect's own changes are checked as they happen. The engine checks after each counter placement and after each part of a composite effect, so units an 'each unit' effect kills (Pestilent Titan) die one at a time, not together.

sides.quote: safe point — the engine's state-based check. The end of every action is a safe
because `addCounters` runs `checkDeaths` and a lethal poison hit would otherwise
this.checkDeaths();   // sequential within the composite; triggers wait for settle()
When I attack or block, [Switch1] Put a -1/-1 counter on each unit. Each player gains a rot.

resolution: The rule states the engine's behaviour with basis engine. Question for the owner only if the judge's CR has an 'each unit' effect finish before any death is checked, so that units it kills die together (effects.state.together).
